title: Orbit Race
premise: A neon sci-fi reskin of a two-side Ludo race where the player commands a red pilot squad against a blue AI, launching tokens from base, circling a shared track, capturing rivals, and rushing back to home orbit.
interaction_model: Turn-based board game played with pointer/touch input: the player taps the die to roll, then taps one highlighted token to move while the blue AI takes automated turns.
objective: Get all four red tokens from home, around the outer track, through the red home stretch, and into the center finish before the blue AI finishes all four of its tokens.
progression: Single-match progression with repeated alternating turns, dice-gated token deployment on sixes, captures that reset enemy progress, extra turns on rolling six, and a final win screen when one side finishes all four tokens.
theme: Arcade space-race board duel with orbital, pilot, neon, and mission-control framing.
mood: Bright, competitive, lightweight, and family-friendly with flashy sci-fi feedback.
likely_audience: players who enjoy simplified Ludo-style competition
confidence_notes: High confidence that the underlying ruleset is a simplified two-player Ludo variant because of the 15x15 board, four tokens per side, roll-of-6 deployment, shared loop path, captures sending tokens home, and dedicated home stretches.
High confidence in the space-race presentation because the UI text, feedback phrases, token art, and background all consistently frame the board as an orbit mission.
Moderate confidence on the intended title because the HTML title says 'Ludo Royale' while the on-screen branding presents the game as 'ORBIT Race'; the in-game identity appears to be Orbit Race.
recreation_prompt: Create a polished single-screen browser game that plays like a two-player Ludo match reimagined as a neon sci-fi orbit race. The player controls a red pilot squad against a blue AI on a centered 15x15 board drawn on canvas, with four tokens per side, a shared outer loop path, separate home bases, player-specific home stretches, and a central finish. Start with a cinematic overlay showing a futuristic title, short mission text, and a start button. During play, show a compact glassmorphism HUD with a large die in the top center, red and blue side labels, and a turn indicator. The human player taps or clicks the die to roll, then taps a highlighted valid red token to move it; the blue side is an automated opponent that rolls and chooses randomly among valid moves. Use core Ludo-like rules: tokens begin in home, a roll of 6 is required to launch a token onto the track, moving onto an opponent’s track space sends that enemy token back home, rolling a 6 grants another turn, entering the final home stretch only happens near the end of the loop, and a side wins by getting all four tokens to the finish. Present everything with a glossy arcade space aesthetic: deep navy starfield background, glowing red and blue route accents, rounded UI cards, futuristic fonts, animated status messages, reaction visuals for captures and blocked turns, and energetic audio for rolling, moving, captures, blocked turns, start, and victory. Keep the match readable, responsive, and touch-friendly, with simple casual AI and an end screen that clearly announces whether the red pilot or blue AI wins.
